A1.justification: Both PDFs describe P-CHECK. All 24 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, appendices, and prompts, support comparison. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-prediction and personalized-generation experiments, ablations, robustness tests, and checklist-quality evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds threshold-sensitivity, chronological-history, and generator-backbone evaluations.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.5 retain the same checklist construction, contrastive sampling, saliency weighting, training objective, and reward computation. The additional backbone and streaming experiments apply this existing procedure.

E1.justification: PRISM, Arena, and BESPOKE coverage is retained. Appendix A.2.2 adds a PRISM scenario with chronologically growing histories, testing prediction under changing available user context rather than the existing static-history evaluations.

E2.justification: The new streaming comparison in Table 8 evaluates a persona-based judge using the same per-turn updated persona as P-CHECK, without checklist generation. Comparator membership in the existing main experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The new streaming protocol uses only history through turn t−1, updates summaries each turn, restricts users to at least eight turns, and evaluates four chronological quarters. Additional experiments sweep saliency thresholds and train Qwen-3-4B and Gemma-3-4B generators with a fixed Llama3-8B judge. Existing experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted checks of training-label threshold sensitivity (Table 5), chronological-history robustness (Table 8), and generator-family dependence (Table 9). Existing component ablations, numerical-weight sensitivity, sparse-history tests, cost analysis, checklist evaluation, and case studies remain.

E5.justification: Five-run reporting, 95% confidence intervals, and paired t-tests for personalized generation are retained. The new appendix tables report point estimates, consistent with existing appendix tables, without introducing new seed, run-count, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–4 retain their numerical results. New results include threshold-sweep accuracies of 63.27–65.89%, Q4 streaming accuracy of 61.33% versus 56.20% for the persona baseline, and Qwen-3-4B generator accuracies of 66.48% on PRISM and 63.55% on Arena. These are additional experimental conditions, not revised headline scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1–7 are unchanged, including saliency, cumulative-threshold labeling, the training objective, and weighted reward aggregation. No new theorem, proof, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about dynamic personalized checklists, preference-contrastive weighting, reward accuracy, downstream generation, and OOD robustness. Contribution-bullet edits do not change their scientific meaning.

C2.justification: New appendix discussion interprets updated summaries as enabling adaptation to preference shift and the backbone results as evidence of portability across generator families. The drift interpretation relies on chronological quarters without directly measuring preference change. Existing limitations and failure-case explanations are retained.

D1.justification: The added analyses document chronological history construction, per-turn summary updates, alternative generator identities, and the fixed downstream judge. The original implementation details, training hyperparameters, hardware, prompts, and code-access destination remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Seo et al. (2024) to the hallucination discussion and references. The extended related-work subsections from v1 Appendix A.1 are moved into Section 5 with their substantive positioning preserved.

P1.justification: v2 integrates the extended related work into the main text, renumbers appendix sections, lightly edits contribution bullets, and adds department, corresponding-author, and acknowledgement text. Most existing prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5, 8, and 9 and reflows subsequent appendix displays. Figure 8 revises percentage-axis labeling, including adding the lower panel's 60% tick and repositioning its other ticks. Existing figures and tables otherwise retain their designs.

improvement.justification: Table 9 provides useful evidence that effectiveness extends beyond the original generator family, and Figure 8 improves quantitative readability while the core evidence is preserved. These provide a limited net gain. The added checks have reporting weaknesses: Table 5's label proportions conflict with Section 3.4's threshold rule, while Table 8 repeats Q4 values as unexplained macro averages and does not directly establish preference drift.
